europmc-pmc6692429: NF-kB is inflammation's master switch - but what is it doing inside mitochondria, the cell's power plants? This review gathers the scattered evidence on NF-kB's mitochondrial cameo: a familiar protein in an unfamiliar place. The cameo may link immunity, energy, and disease in unexpected ways.
europmc-pmc6747329: Everyone 'knows' metastases cause 90% of cancer deaths - but nobody checked. Using population data from a Norwegian cancer registry, this study measured what share of deaths metastases truly cause. The myth-busting result resets one of oncology's most quoted statistics.
europmc-pmc6853829: Ovarian cancer is the most lethal women's tumor - silent until late. This review maps its present state and plans for lifting treatment outcomes: the screening gap, new care, and what's next. Early detection stays the big prize. Catching it early would save the most lives.
europmc-pmc6855329: Not every heart attack comes from a burst plaque. This paper tackles workup and care of type 2 myocardial infarction and sudden nonischemic myocardial injury: the heart attacks with other causes. The overlooked MIs at last get their manual. Different cause, different cure - know the difference.
europmc-pmc6858629: Checkpoint drugs free the immune system - at times against the body. This review links immune-related bad events to anti-tumor power of checkpoint blockers: the side effects that flag success. The own-goal fire may mark the wins. Harm and wins, two sides of one coin.
europmc-pmc6859529: The cell's protein factory runs on careful chemistry - and stress breaks the line. This review shows how redox signaling and the unfolded protein response coordinate cell fate under ER stress. The factory's alarm system decides: fix or self-destruct. Fold right, or die trying.
europmc-pmc6882729: The garden strawberry is a gene octuple-merger - eight chromosome sets. This study mapped the birth and history of the eightfold strawberry DNA with a near-complete map. The berry knotted roots are now mapped. 8 sets, one tasty fruit.
europmc-pmc6882829: t-SNE plots are everywhere in single-cell biology - and often misread. This paper is the art of using t-SNE for single-cell transcriptomics: what the pretty blobs mean and what they don't. The field guide to honest visualization. Beautiful plots, careful conclusions.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-29: Published in 2007 by the Government Accountability Office, this report examines safety on airport runways and ramp areas. It reviews leadership gaps, technology shortfalls, and other challenges that contribute to accidents and near-misses where aircraft operate on the ground. The report calls for sustained effort across agencies to reduce runway incursions and ground collisions, and it grades the federal response to a long-standing aviation safety problem.
gao-gaoreports-b-299929: A second 2007 GAO ruling for AlliedBarton Security Services LLC — three more contract fights, same year, same firm. The guard company kept challenging federal awards, and GAO kept the calls coming. Read with its twin ruling, the pair maps how the government buys guard work — and how hard the big firms fight for it.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1129: A reactor-building boom was brewing in 2007, and GAO checked whether the atom referees were ready. The Nuclear Regulatory Commission's licensing gears and staffing mostly passed, GAO found — but big unknowns hung over the coming flood of plant bids. The report tests the safety watchdog on the eve of its busiest stretch in decades.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-629: The IRS's own audit report card came due in 2007 — GAO's letter tracks the financial audit and the fixes still owed. The findings keep the tax agency's books under a watchful eye. The letter's premise: the collector must itself be beyond reproach.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-729: Foreign airports got American report cards in 2007 — GAO's report says overseas assessments and carrier inspections lifted security, but the watch needed work. The findings balance credit and caution. The report's reach: the sky has no borders, so neither should the screening.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-29: Credit unions needed more sunlight in 2007, and GAO's report says transparency was lacking on who they served and what bosses earned. The findings demand the disclosure. The report warns that the member-owned banks should act like it. The books had to open.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-1029: Nuclear plant oversight was improving in 2006, and GAO's report says the regulator's watch had gotten better, though refinements were needed. The findings balance credit and caution. The report warns that the reactors deserved relentless vigilance. The watch could not blink.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-929: Credit card fine print was getting trickier in 2006, and GAO's report says the growing complexity heightened the need for clearer disclosures. The findings demand the plain talk. The report warns that the plastic's traps needed sunlight. The disclosures had to be honest.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-829: America's overseas footprint needed consolidating in 2006, and GAO's report says State and USAID should adopt a comprehensive support plan. The findings demand the blueprint. The report warns that the scattered outposts needed joining up. The presence had to be efficient.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-629: Geothermal energy faced hurdles in 2006, and GAO's report says increased development would depend on overcoming many challenges. The findings map the obstacles. The report warns that the earth's heat was free but hard to tap. The challenges had to be overcome.
gao-gaoreports-b-307529: The Capitol Police's erroneous salary payments got a waiver ruling in this March 2006 GAO call, which tests forgiving the overpayments. The decision reads the money law. The ruling decides whether the mistaken paychecks could be forgiven. The law had the final word.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-429: The pension backstop's books needed daylight in 2006, and GAO's report says the reporting could be clearer. The findings target the fog. The report warns that the retirees' safety net deserved open books. The books had to be open. The safety net deserved clear books.
openalex-w7204279629: Maps can be acts of resistance. This article tells how the riverside community of Curupere Grande in Para mapped its own territory through social cartography, recording land, livelihood, and memory. The authors describe the project born from a geotechnology course. A vivid account of a traditional community drawing its own lines.
openalex-w7119516229: Potassium ions drift through water in ways that matter for batteries and biology. This paper studies their diffusion with pulsed-field gradient NMR, a magnetic technique that tracks molecular motion. The authors tackle the method's limits for these fast ions. A physical-chemistry study of salt on the move.
openalex-w7204785729: Glass that turns blue light into ultraviolet could serve sensors and sterilizers. This paper reports praseodymium-doped silica glasses, melted while levitating, emitting strong UV under blue excitation. The authors pushed past normal doping limits. A photonics study of glass that upgrades light.
arxiv-2606-16229: Program analyzers use "abstract transformers" to reason about what code can do without running it. This paper shows how to automatically synthesize the best such transformers using parallel bit-vector optimization — searching many possibilities at once. It targets researchers in program analysis and formal verification of software.
arxiv-2606-16429: Slim mind-frames vow big-brain smarts at small cost — yet brew them from giants and the first pour sets the brew. Taylor-Calibrate picks that first pour by slope-math, so slim frames start true. For crews who press giants into slim molds.
arxiv-2606-16529: Count-math has a storied span from clockwork to quirk. This paper runs that span over twist-space (contact 3-folds) and ties it to a 'Reeb pull field.' Bridge math for curve pros and sum sages. Spans like this turn old rules new.
arxiv-2606-16729: Reinforcement learning agents usually need tons of trial runs. This paper asks: can an agent learn a good policy from just ONE trajectory (a single run) in average-reward settings — where what matters is the long-run average payoff? It is a learning-theory result for RL researchers.
